passages.author: Julian of Eclanum
passages.text: By both our practice and our speech, we testify that everyone must be reborn through baptism. But this benefit is not bestowed so that people seem to have been kidnapped from the devil’s rightful possession. Rather, those who are God’s works become God’s children; those born in a lowly condition, but not a guilty one, are reborn at great worth, but without a false accusation. Those who come forth from God’s institutions are advanced by God’s mysteries; those who bring nature’s works receive grace’s gifts. Their Lord, who made them good by creating them, makes them better by renewing and adopting them. You must therefore confess that it is rightly said that the natural sin Mani invented, which you call original sin with a change of name, has perished. passages.text: You located salvation in baptism and argued consistently that if the Manichaeans, who call nature evil, spoke truly, Christians would be foolish to believe baptism’s remedy should be applied to an evil nature. sign-and-seal.quote: reborn through the washing
sign-and-seal.audited: 'ὁ δὲ μόνον βαπτισθεὶς εἰ καὶ μήπω ἔσχεν ἐνάρετον βίον ὑπὲρ τὸν Ἰωάννην ἐστίν' (even one only baptized, without a virtuous life yet, is above John) treats every baptized person as in the reborn state.

ordinance-symbol.quote: the believer reborn through the washing
ordinance-symbol.audited: 'reborn through the washing' (διὰ τοῦ λουτροῦ ἀναγεννηθέντα) is the exact exclusion.

passages.attribution_note: A catena fragment: the ascription rests on the catena heading and is not secure.

passages.author: Cyril of Alexandria
passages.text: self the type of the holy baptism, washing us with holy waters unto putting-away of sin, and carrying off unto the kingdom of the heavens. And from-above and from heaven is the holy baptism; and a riddle of this, the hyacinth color. Or do I not seem to you to say these things best, as at least in such hard-to-grasp of contemplations?

regeneration.quote: washing us with holy waters unto putting‑away of sin, and carrying off unto the kingdom of the heavens
regeneration.audited: 'the holy baptism, washing us with holy waters unto putting-away of sin, and carrying off unto the kingdom of the heavens'.

ordinance-symbol.quote: washing us with holy waters unto putting-away of sin
ordinance-symbol.audited: 'washing us with holy waters unto putting-away of sin' is the exact exclusion.

passages.author: Cyril of Alexandria
passages.text: We approach the grace of holy baptism, which sanctifies us and gives us the power to remove sins and be reborn spiritually, conforming us to Christ. This baptism also gives us a bold entrance into the kingdom of heaven, as Jesus said, 'Unless one is born of water and spirit, they cannot enter the kingdom of God.' The Jews, however, lack this gift, for they do not have the power of bread, which is the life-giving power in Christ, nor do they have the power of water.

regeneration.quote: sanctifies us and gives us the power to remove sins and be reborn spiritually
regeneration.audited: Greek: 'ὕδατος τὴν ἰσχὺν εἶναι λέγοντες ἁμαρτιῶν ἀπόθεσιν, ἀναγέννησιν τὴν πνευματικὴν' (saying the power of the water is the putting-off of sins, spiritual rebirth). Fidelity: the English 'which is necessary for spiritual rebirth' is not in the Greek, which says 'they do not have the power of water; for sin remains among them unwashed'.

sign-and-seal.quote: sanctifies us and gives us the power to remove sins and be reborn spiritually
sign-and-seal.audited: Cyril on Isaiah: 'the grace of holy baptism, which sanctifies us and gives us the power to remove sins and be reborn spiritually, conforming us to Christ... a bold entrance into the kingdom of heaven, as Jesus said, Unless one is born of water and spirit, they cannot enter the kingdom of God' (John 3:5) - baptism itself sanctifies and rebirths, tied to the necessity of John 3:5; no room for a seal whose grace is deferred or selective.

ordinance-symbol.quote: sanctifies us and gives us the power to remove sins and be reborn spiritually
ordinance-symbol.audited: 'the power of the water is the putting-off of sins, spiritual rebirth' is the exact exclusion.

passages.author: Hesychius of Jerusalem
passages.text: 'And living water will come out of Jerusalem.' From where? From the side of the living one; for just as Eve was formed, there the church is likewise formed. 'The half of it into the first sea'—that is a sign of baptism. 'And the half of it into the last sea'—this is clearly a sign of repentance. For the tears of repentance are a remnant of the gift of baptism, a clear proof: for one who has not been baptized repents in vain if he does not run to be baptized; in vain he offers prayer, in vain he asks for forgiveness, in vain he sheds tears. For without baptism, the forgiveness of sins is not granted. But one who has been baptized has effective repentance: he weeps and is loosed, he sighs and mourns and prays, and he is immediately cleansed.

regeneration.quote: without baptism, the forgiveness of sins is not granted... he is immediately cleansed
regeneration.audited: Greek: 'Χωρὶς γὰρ βαπτίσματος ἄφεσις ἁμαρτημάτων οὐ πράττεται' (without baptism forgiveness of sins is not granted); faithful.

sign-and-seal.quote: without baptism, the forgiveness of sins is not granted
sign-and-seal.audited: 'ὁ μὴ βαπτισθεὶς μάτην μετανοεῖ ... Χωρὶς βαπτίσματος ἄφεσις οὐ πράττεται' ties forgiveness strictly to baptism, which Westminster 28.5 (the position's defined quote) denies.

ordinance-symbol.quote: without baptism, the forgiveness of sins is not granted
ordinance-symbol.audited: 'without baptism, the forgiveness of sins is not granted' makes baptism the means of forgiveness.

passages.author: Ammonius of Alexandria
passages.text: ; but John’s baptism gave forgiveness of voluntary sins to those truly repenting, and Christ’s of all sins, and also supplied Holy Spirit and the dignity of adoption.

regeneration.quote: Christ's [baptism] of all sins, and also supplied Holy Spirit and the dignity of adoption
regeneration.audited: Ammonius, fragment on John: 'John's baptism gave forgiveness of voluntary sins to those truly repenting, and Christ's of all sins, and also supplied Holy Spirit and the dignity of adoption' - Christ's baptism itself forgives all sins and supplies the Spirit and adoption.

sign-and-seal.quote: Christ's [baptism] of all sins, and also supplied Holy Spirit and the dignity of adoption
sign-and-seal.audited: The effects are predicated of Christ's baptism as such - forgiveness 'of all sins,' the Holy Spirit supplied, adoption given - located in the rite, without the election or timing qualifications this position requires.

ordinance-symbol.quote: Christ's [baptism] of all sins, and also supplied Holy Spirit and the dignity of adoption
ordinance-symbol.audited: A baptism that itself forgives all sins and supplies the Spirit and adoption conveys grace; it does not merely picture a salvation already received.

passages.attribution_note: A catena fragment: the ascription rests on the catena heading and is not secure.

passages.author: Ammonius of Alexandria
passages.text: He is a lamb as given for forgiveness of sins of those being regenerated “through washing of rebirth” (Titus 3:5); and by saying “taking away” he shows that he always takes away.

regeneration.quote: through washing of rebirth
regeneration.audited: Ammonius: Christ is 'given for forgiveness of sins of those being regenerated through washing of rebirth (Titus 3:5)' - regeneration runs through the washing; the washing is its instrument.

ordinance-symbol.quote: through washing of rebirth
ordinance-symbol.audited: Regeneration 'through washing of rebirth' contradicts a washing that only pictures a completed regeneration.

passages.attribution_note: A catena fragment: the ascription rests on the catena heading and is not secure.

passages.author: Ammonius of Alexandria
passages.text: Water cleanses the body and the Spirit sanctifies the invisible soul. Water is taken in the place of a mother, and the Spirit in the place of God who forms. Sensible water is re-elemented toward divine power and sanctifies those in whom rebirth happens. Water differs from Spirit only in conception, since it is the same in activity; water is a symbol of burial and resurrection, and therefore is necessarily taken. Three immersions and three emergings happen so that we may know that by power of Father and Son and Holy Spirit all is fulfilled.

regeneration.audited: Ammonius: 'Sensible water is re-elemented toward divine power and sanctifies those in whom rebirth happens. Water differs from Spirit only in conception, since it is the same in activity... water is a symbol of burial and resurrection, and therefore is necessarily taken' - the water actively sanctifies and is the same in activity as the Spirit in the rebirth. Downgrades the grader's compatible (disputed).

sign-and-seal.audited: The water is 'necessarily taken' and itself sanctifies those in whom rebirth happens, 'the same in activity' as the Spirit - operative in the act itself, with no distinction between elect and non-elect or deferred grace.

ordinance-symbol.quote: Sensible water is re-elemented toward divine power and sanctifies those in whom rebirth happens
ordinance-symbol.audited: Water that sanctifies and is 'necessarily taken' is a symbol with efficacy, not a symbol instead of efficacy - it conveys the sanctification it figures.

passages.attribution_note: A catena fragment: the ascription rests on the catena heading and is not secure.

passages.author: Ammonius of Alexandria
passages.text: Through baptism Christ betroths the church reborn. This spiritual yoke joins to God through the teaching word. The bride is a pure virgin through rightness of doctrines; she is also Christ’s wife as bearing good deeds not from herself but through Christ who sows in her—of whom none of the generated can be bridegroom, since none of them is primarily giver of goods. So every rational nature of angels and humans is bride.

ordinance-symbol.quote: Through baptism Christ betroths the church reborn.
ordinance-symbol.audited: Ammonius: 'Through baptism Christ betroths the church reborn' - baptism is the through-means by which the church is reborn and betrothed; a means of rebirth, not a testimony to a rebirth already complete.

passages.attribution_note: A catena fragment: the ascription rests on the catena heading and is not secure.

passages.author: Ammonius of Alexandria
passages.text: The one living the upper life of the angels and learning high doctrines through Christ is born from above. The one undergoing the second birth through the washing is born from above, and the one partaking of Holy Spirit. “From above” signifies rebirth through the Spirit and shows that the Spirit is from the Father’s essence; for thus, naming himself also from above, he signifies that he is from the Father’s essence.

regeneration.quote: the one undergoing the second birth through the washing is born from above
regeneration.audited: Ammonius: 'The one undergoing the second birth through the washing is born from above, and the one partaking of Holy Spirit' - the second birth comes through the washing.

sign-and-seal.quote: the one undergoing the second birth through the washing is born from above
sign-and-seal.audited: 'The one undergoing the second birth through the washing IS born from above' - the new birth is predicated of the washed as such and located in the washing, without election or timing qualification.

ordinance-symbol.quote: the one undergoing the second birth through the washing is born from above
ordinance-symbol.audited: A second birth through the washing is a birth baptism effects, not a portrait of a birth already received.

passages.attribution_note: A catena fragment: the ascription rests on the catena heading and is not secure.

passages.author: Ammonius of Alexandria
passages.text: Christ is bridegroom and the church bride and the bridal chamber the place of baptism, where spiritual joining happens, since all is bright and full of joy and gladness. For what is more blessed than to be cleansed of sins and cleave to God and “become partaker of divine nature” (2 Peter 1:4) through sharing the Holy Spirit? These are the earnest; the more perfect things are in the future, when the bridegroom enters again and brings with him the virgin souls and the bridal door is shut and only those inside enjoy the gladness and no one enters there anymore. So as long as today’s age, or each one’s particular death, the bridal door is open to souls willing to be betrothed to Christ.

regeneration.quote: to be cleansed of sins and cleave to God and 'become partaker of divine nature' through sharing the Holy Spirit
regeneration.audited: Ammonius: the bridal chamber is 'the place of baptism, where spiritual joining happens... to be cleansed of sins and cleave to God and become partaker of divine nature (2 Peter 1:4) through sharing the Holy Spirit' - cleansing from sins and divine participation happen in baptism.

ordinance-symbol.quote: to be cleansed of sins and cleave to God and 'become partaker of divine nature' through sharing the Holy Spirit
ordinance-symbol.audited: Cleansing, cleaving to God, and partaking of the divine nature are baptism's own fruits - not a picture of fruits already possessed.

questions.question: How is the Church governed, and who ordains its ministers?
shared_ground: There are ordained ministers called elders or presbyters, and deacons
Ordination by laying on of hands with prayer
The congregation has a part in choosing or approving its ministers
Church discipline is exercised
Councils of bishops met to settle disputes (as a historical fact, without a claim about divine institution)

positions.name: Bishops in apostolic succession

defined.source: Catechism of the Catholic Church, 77
defined.quote: In order that the full and living Gospel might always be preserved in the Church the apostles left bishops as their successors.

defined.source: Confession of Dositheus (Synod of Jerusalem), Decree 10 (1672)
defined.quote: he, as a successor of the Apostles, having received in continued succession by the imposition of hands and the invocation of the All-holy Spirit the grace that is given him of the Lord of binding and loosing

defined.source: Book of Common Prayer, Preface to the Ordinal (1662)
defined.quote: It is evident unto all men diligently reading holy Scripture and ancient Authors, that from the Apostles' time there have been these Orders of Ministers in Christ's Church; Bishops, Priests, and Deacons.

defined.source: CopticChurch.net, Sacraments: Priesthood
defined.quote: the service of Patriarchs, successors of the Apostles everywhere, at all times

defined.source: Common Statement on Sacramental Life, Catholic Church and Assyrian Church of the East (2017)
defined.quote: The requirement that all ordained ministers of the Church should stand in the apostolic succession, in virtue of their sacramental ordination, is an expression and a guarantee of continuity between the apostolic origin of the Church and the present qualification of her ministers.

positions.statement: Bishops, distinct from and above presbyters, succeed the apostles through an unbroken line of ordination, and govern the churches.
positions.mark: The passage places one bishop over presbyters and deacons as successor of the apostles, or traces bishops in a line from the apostles.
positions.first_defined: Not a single dogma; Council of Trent, Session 23 (1563); Anglican Ordinal (1550/1662); Synod of Jerusalem (1672)

first_states.author: Ignatius of Antioch
first_states.text: Every one of you, follow the bishop, as Jesus Christ follows the Father. Follow the presbytery as you would the apostles. Honor the deacons as you would God's own command. Let no one do anything that belongs to the church without the bishop. Let that Eucharist be held valid which is under the bishop, or under someone he has entrusted with it. Where the bishop appears, there let the people be, just as where Jesus Christ is, there is the catholic church. Without the bishop it is not permitted either to baptize or to hold the love feast. But whatever he approves is pleasing to God as well, so that everything you do may be sure and valid.

episcopal-succession.quote: Follow the bishop, as Jesus Christ follows the Father. Follow the presbytery as you would the apostles.
episcopal-succession.audited: Smyrnaeans 8: follow the bishop as Christ follows the Father and the presbytery as the apostles; let no one do anything of the church without the bishop; the Eucharist is valid only under him and baptism is not permitted without him - one bishop over presbyters and deacons, with the church's acts depending on him.

presbyterian.quote: Where the bishop appears, there let the people be... Without the bishop it is not permitted either to baptize or to hold the love feast.
presbyterian.audited: The bishop alone validates the sacraments; the presbytery follows as apostles under his headship.

congregational.quote: Let no one do anything that belongs to the church without the bishop.
congregational.audited: 'Let no one do anything that belongs to the church without the bishop.'

positions.name: Equal presbyters governing in councils

defined.source: Belgic Confession, Article 31 (1561)
defined.quote: As for the ministers of the Word, they all have the same power and authority, no matter where they may be

defined.source: Westminster Confession of Faith, 31.1 (1646)
defined.quote: For the better government, and further edification of the church, there ought to be such assemblies as are commonly called synods or councils

positions.statement: All ministers of the Word hold equal authority; churches are governed by elders, and congregations are joined under assemblies of elders (synods).
positions.mark: The passage says presbyters and bishops are equal in authority, or that churches are governed jointly by a body of elders above the congregation.
positions.first_defined: Belgic Confession (1561); Westminster Confession (1646)

first_states.author: Clement of Rome
first_states.text: Our apostles knew through our Lord Jesus Christ that strife would arise over the office of bishop. For this reason, having received complete foreknowledge, they appointed the men mentioned above and gave instructions that if they should die, other approved men would succeed to their ministry. We do not consider it right to remove from their ministry those who were appointed by them, or later by other reputable men with the consent of the whole church. These men have served the flock of Christ blamelessly, with humility, quietly and without arrogance, and have been well spoken of by all for many years. It would be no small sin for us to depose those who have offered the gifts of the episcopacy blamelessly and piously. Blessed are the elders who have gone before us, who experienced a fruitful and complete departure; they do not fear that anyone will displace them from the place established

presbyterian.audited: 1 Clement 44: the same men are called bishops - their ministry is named 'the episcopacy' - and elders; one shared ministry with no higher episcopal order, which is the interchangeability this position claims.

congregational.quote: appointed by them, or later by other reputable men with the consent of the whole church
congregational.audited: Appointment is by the apostles or 'other reputable men,' the congregation only consenting, and deposing blameless presbyters is sin - officers are not the congregation's to install or remove at will.

positions.name: Self-governing congregation

defined.source: Second London Baptist Confession, 26.7 (1689)
defined.quote: To each of these churches thus gathered, according to his mind declared in his word, he hath given all that power and authority, which is in any way needful for their carrying on that order in worship and discipline

defined.source: Baptist Faith and Message, Article VI (2000)
defined.quote: A New Testament church of the Lord Jesus Christ is an autonomous local congregation of baptized believers, associated by covenant in the faith and fellowship of the gospel

positions.statement: Each gathered congregation holds full authority from Christ to choose its officers and exercise discipline, with no higher church body over it.
positions.mark: The passage says a local congregation holds full authority in itself, with no bishop or synod above it.
positions.first_defined: Cambridge Platform (1648); Second London Baptist Confession, ch. 26 (1689)

passages.author: Clement of Rome
passages.text: Take up the letter of the blessed apostle Paul and consider what he wrote to you at the very beginning of the gospel. He truly wrote to you under the Spirit's guidance about himself, Cephas, and Apollos, because even then you had formed factions. But that division brought you a lesser sin, since you were aligning yourselves with apostles who had been testified to and with a man approved by them. Now consider who has led you astray and diminished the noble character of your renowned brotherly love. It is shameful, beloved, utterly shameful, and unworthy of the conduct that belongs to life in Christ, that the most established and ancient church of the Corinthians should be in rebellion against its presbyters because of one or two persons. This report has reached not only us, but also those who differ from us, so that blasphemies are heaped on the Lord's name because of your folly, and you

congregational.quote: …the most established and ancient church of the Corinthians should be in rebellion against its presbyters…
congregational.audited: 1 Clement 47 brands the congregation's removal of its presbyters rebellion and folly, and Rome instructs Corinth from outside; no full congregational authority.

passages.author: Ignatius of Antioch
passages.text: Be subject to the bishop and to one another, as Jesus Christ was subject to the Father and the apostles were subject to Christ and to the Father, so that there may be a unity that is both fleshly and spiritual.

presbyterian.quote: Be subject to the bishop …
presbyterian.audited: 'Be subject to the bishop... as Jesus Christ was subject to the Father' - submission runs to the bishop, not to a body of equal elders.

congregational.quote: Be subject to the bishop
congregational.audited: The same command subordinates the whole church to the bishop.

passages.author: Ignatius of Antioch
passages.text: The Lord was united with the Father, and so he did nothing without the Father, neither by himself nor through the apostles. In the same way, you must do nothing without the bishop and the council of elders. Do not even try to make anything appear reasonable to you privately. Instead, gather together in one place and have one prayer, one supplication, one mind, one hope in love, in the blameless joy, which is Jesus Christ, than whom nothing is better.

congregational.quote: you must do nothing without the bishop and the council of elders
congregational.audited: Magnesians 2.7: 'you must do nothing without the bishop and the council of elders.'

passages.author: Ignatius of Antioch
passages.text: In the same way, let everyone respect the deacons as they would Jesus Christ, just as they should also respect the bishop, who is a pattern of the Father, and the council of elders as the council of God and as a bond of the apostles. Without these, a church is not called a church.

congregational.quote: Without these, a church is not called a church
congregational.audited: Trallians 3.3: respect the bishop, 'who is a pattern of the Father,' and the council of elders 'as a bond of the apostles'; 'without these, a church is not called a church.'

passages.text: All of you follow the bishop, as Jesus Christ followed the Father, and follow the council of elders as you would the apostles. Respect the deacons as God's command. Let no one do anything that pertains to the church without the bishop. Let that Eucharist be considered valid which is under the bishop or under someone he has entrusted.

episcopal-succession.quote: follow the bishop, as Jesus Christ followed the Father, and follow the council of elders as you would the apostles
episcopal-succession.audited: Smyrnaeans 8 (letters text): follow the bishop as Christ followed the Father and the council of elders as the apostles; no church act and no valid Eucharist apart from the bishop or the one he has entrusted.

presbyterian.quote: Let no one do anything that pertains to the church without the bishop
presbyterian.audited: Sole episcopal authorization replaces collegial elder rule.

congregational.quote: Let no one do anything that pertains to the church without the bishop
congregational.audited: 'Let no one do anything that pertains to the church without the bishop.'

passages.author: Ignatius of Antioch
passages.text: So it is necessary, as you are already doing, that you do nothing without the bishop. Submit also to the council of elders as you would to the apostles of Jesus Christ our hope, in whom we will be found if we live in him.

presbyterian.quote: do nothing without the bishop
presbyterian.audited: Trallians 3: 'do nothing without the bishop; submit also to the council of elders as you would to the apostles' - the bishop holds the first and distinct authority.

congregational.quote: do nothing without the bishop
congregational.audited: Nothing may be done without the bishop.

passages.author: Ignatius of Antioch
passages.text: In a short time I came to know your bishop with a closeness that was not human but spiritual. If that is true of me, how much more do I count you blessed, who are joined with him as the church is joined with Jesus Christ, and as Jesus Christ is joined with the Father, so that all things may sound together in unity? Let no one be deceived. Anyone who is not within the altar goes without the bread of God. For if the prayer of one or two carries such power, how much more the prayer of the bishop and the whole church? So whoever stays away from the assembly is already proud and has passed sentence on himself. For it is written, "God opposes the proud" (Proverbs 3:34; James 4:6; 1 Peter 5:5). Let us be eager, then, not to oppose the bishop, so that we may be subject to God.

congregational.quote: Let us be eager, then, not to oppose the bishop, so that we may be subject to God
congregational.audited: Ephesians 5: 'not to oppose the bishop, so that we may be subject to God'; whoever is outside the altar is deprived and self-condemned.

passages.author: Ignatius of Antioch
passages.text: Likewise, let everyone honor the deacons as Jesus Christ, and the bishop too, for he is a figure of the Father, and the presbyters as God's council and the apostles' band. Without these, nothing is called a church. I am sure you feel the same about all this. For I have received the sample of your love, and I keep it with me in your bishop. His very bearing is a great lesson, and his gentleness is power. I think even the godless honor him. Because I love you, I spare you, though I could write more sharply on this point. I did not think myself fit for this, that I, a condemned man, should issue you commands like an apostle.

congregational.quote: Without these, nothing is called a church
congregational.audited: Trallians 3: the bishop is 'a figure of the Father,' the presbyters 'God's council and the apostles' band'; 'without these, nothing is called a church.'

passages.author: Ignatius of Antioch
passages.text: The Lord was one with the Father and did nothing without him (John 5:19): nothing on his own, nothing through the apostles. In the same way, you must do nothing without the bishop and the presbyters. Do not try to make some private course look reasonable to yourselves. Come together in one place: one prayer, one plea, one mind, one hope, in love, in spotless joy. That joy is Jesus Christ, and nothing is better than he. Run together, all of you, as to one temple of God, as to one altar, to one Jesus Christ. He came forth from one Father; he is with that One; and to that One he has returned.

congregational.quote: Do nothing without the bishop and the presbyters. Do not try to make some private course look reasonable to yourselves.
congregational.audited: Magnesians 7: 'do nothing without the bishop and the presbyters; do not try to make some private course look reasonable to yourselves.'

passages.author: Ignatius of Antioch
passages.text: Wherever the bishop appears, there let the congregation be, just as wherever Jesus Christ is, there is the whole church. It is not permitted to baptize or to hold a love-feast without the bishop. But whatever he approves, this is also pleasing to God, so that everything you do may be secure and valid.

episcopal-succession.quote: Wherever the bishop appears, there let the congregation be, just as wherever Jesus Christ is, there is the whole church.

presbyterian.quote: Wherever the bishop appears, there let the congregation be... whatever he approves, this is also pleasing to God
presbyterian.audited: Sacramental validity hangs on the one bishop, not on a body of elders acting together.

congregational.quote: It is not permitted to baptize or to hold a love-feast without the bishop.
congregational.audited: 'It is not permitted to baptize or to hold a love-feast without the bishop.'

passages.author: Ignatius of Antioch
passages.text: The more anyone sees a bishop keeping silent, the more let him stand in awe of him. Whoever the Master of the house sends to run his household, we must welcome as we would welcome the one who sent him (Matthew 10:40; John 13:20). Plainly, then, we must regard the bishop as the Lord himself. Onesimus himself warmly praises your good order in God. You all live by the truth, and no faction makes its home among you. In fact, you do not even listen to anyone more than to one who speaks truly about Jesus Christ.

congregational.quote: we must regard the bishop as the Lord himself
congregational.audited: Ephesians 6: the bishop sent to run the household must be regarded 'as the Lord himself.'

passages.author: Ignatius of Antioch
passages.text: In the persons I have named I have looked on your whole congregation in faith, and I have loved it. So I urge you: be eager to do everything in God's own harmony, with the bishop presiding in the place of God, the presbyters in the place of the council of the apostles, and the deacons, so very dear to me, entrusted with the ministry of Jesus Christ, who was with the Father before the ages and at the end was revealed. All of you, then, having received God's own character, respect one another. Let no one regard his neighbor according to the flesh; love one another in Jesus Christ, always. Let nothing be among you that could divide you. Be one with the bishop and with those who preside, as a pattern and a lesson of incorruption.

episcopal-succession.quote: the bishop presiding in the place of God, the presbyters in the place of the council of the apostles
episcopal-succession.audited: Magnesians 6: 'the bishop presiding in the place of God, the presbyters in the place of the council of the apostles, and the deacons entrusted with the ministry of Jesus Christ' - one bishop presiding over presbyters and deacons.

presbyterian.quote: the bishop presiding in the place of God, the presbyters in the place of the council of the apostles
presbyterian.audited: The bishop presides in God's place; the presbyters' place is beneath his presidency.

congregational.quote: Be one with the bishop and with those who preside
congregational.audited: 'Be one with the bishop and with those who preside.'

passages.author: Ignatius of Antioch
passages.text: When you submit to the bishop as you would to Jesus Christ, I can see that you are not living by human standards. You live by Jesus Christ, who died for us so that, believing in his death, you might escape death. So it is necessary, and you already do it, that you undertake nothing apart from the bishop. Submit also to the presbytery as to the apostles of Jesus Christ, our hope. If we make our life in him, in him we will be found. The deacons, too, serve the mysteries of Jesus Christ (1 Corinthians 4:1), and they must please everyone in every way. They are not waiters handing round food and drink; they are servants of God's church. So they must shun every charge against them as they would shun fire.

episcopal-succession.quote: you undertake nothing apart from the bishop. Submit also to the presbytery as to the apostles of Jesus Christ
episcopal-succession.audited: Trallians 2: submit to the bishop as to Jesus Christ and undertake nothing apart from him, while the presbytery is likened to the apostles under him - one bishop over presbyters and deacons in the apostolic ordering of the church.

presbyterian.quote: you undertake nothing apart from the bishop
presbyterian.audited: The bishop is obeyed as Christ while the presbytery stands under the command - no parity.

congregational.quote: you undertake nothing apart from the bishop. Submit also to the presbytery
congregational.audited: Nothing may be undertaken apart from the bishop.

passages.author: Ignatius of Antioch
passages.text: The more you see a bishop keeping silence, the more you should revere him. For everyone whom the master of the house sends to manage his own household, we must receive as we would receive the one who sent him. Clearly, then, we must regard the bishop as the Lord himself.

presbyterian.quote: we must regard the bishop as the Lord himself
presbyterian.audited: Ephesians 1.6: the bishop, sent by the master of the house to manage his household, must be regarded 'as the Lord himself' - a unique representational supremacy over the whole household, not one elder's equal share.

congregational.quote: we must regard the bishop as the Lord himself
congregational.audited: The bishop is received as the Lord himself over the congregation.

passages.author: Ignatius of Antioch
passages.text: You too must not presume on your bishop's youth. According to the power of God the Father, render him every mark of respect. I know that the holy presbyters also have not presumed on his rank, young as it appears. As men wise in God they defer to him; not to him, though, but to the Father of Jesus Christ, the Bishop of all. To honor the One who has desired us, then, it is fitting to obey without any pretense. For a man does not deceive this bishop who is seen; he cheats the Bishop who is unseen. In such a case the reckoning is not with flesh but with God, who knows what is hidden.

presbyterian.quote: "holy presbyters also have not presumed on his rank... As men wise in God they defer to him"
presbyterian.audited: Magnesians 3: the presbyters themselves defer to the bishop's rank, and obedience to him is rendered 'without any pretense' - the presbyters are under the bishop.

congregational.quote: render him every mark of respect... the holy presbyters also have not presumed on his rank... it is fitting to obey without any pretense
congregational.audited: The whole church, presbyters included, owes the bishop unfeigned obedience.

passages.author: Ignatius of Antioch
passages.text: Pay close attention to the bishop, so that God may pay close attention to you. I offer my very life for those who submit to the bishop, the council of elders, and the deacons. May I be counted worthy to have a share with them in God. Labor together, struggle together, run together, suffer together, rest together, and rise together as God's stewards, counselors, and servants.

congregational.quote: Pay close attention to the bishop... submit to the bishop, the council of elders, and the deacons
congregational.audited: Smyrnaeans 7.6 commands submission to the bishop, the council of elders, and the deacons - ordered submission, not self-rule.

passages.author: Ignatius of Antioch
passages.text: Let no one be deceived: if anyone is not within the altar, he is deprived of the bread of God. For if the prayer of one or two has such power, how much more does the prayer of the bishop and of the whole church?

congregational.quote: if anyone is not within the altar, he is deprived of the bread of God
congregational.audited: Ephesians 1.5: whoever is not within the altar is deprived of the bread of God, and the bishop's prayer carries with it the whole church.

passages.author: Ignatius of Antioch
passages.text: Since in the persons I have already named I saw the whole multitude in faith and loved them, I urge you: make it your aim to do everything in the concord of God. Let the bishop preside in the place of God, and the council of elders in the place of the council of the apostles, and let the deacons, who are most sweet to me, be entrusted with the service of Jesus Christ, who before the ages was with the Father and appeared at the end.

episcopal-succession.quote: Let the bishop preside in the place of God, and the council of elders in the place of the council of the apostles
episcopal-succession.audited: Magnesians 2.6: 'let the bishop preside in the place of God, and the council of elders in the place of the council of the apostles' - one bishop presiding over the elders.

presbyterian.quote: Let the bishop preside in the place of God, and the council of elders in the place of the council of the apostles
presbyterian.audited: The bishop presides in God's place over the council of elders.

congregational.quote: Let the bishop preside in the place of God, and the council of elders in the place of the council of the apostles
congregational.audited: The bishop presides over the church in the place of God.

passages.author: Ignatius of Antioch
passages.text: For even if some wished to deceive me according to the flesh, the Spirit is not deceived, for it is from God. It knows where it comes from and where it is going (John 3:8), and it lays bare what is hidden. While I was with you I cried out; I spoke with a loud voice, God's own voice: "Pay attention to the bishop, to the presbytery, and to the deacons." Some suspected that I said this because I already knew of the split among certain people. But the One in whom I am bound is my witness that I did not learn it from human flesh. The Spirit was preaching, saying this: "Do nothing without the bishop. Guard your flesh as God's temple. Love unity. Run from divisions. Become imitators of Jesus Christ, as he is of his Father (1 Corinthians 11:1)."

congregational.quote: Do nothing without the bishop
congregational.audited: Philadelphians 7: 'Do nothing without the bishop' - congregational action requires the bishop.

passages.author: Ignatius of Antioch
passages.text: It is good for us now to come to our senses, while we still have time to repent and turn to God. It is good to know God and the bishop. Whoever honors the bishop has been honored by God. Whoever does anything in secret from the bishop serves the devil.

congregational.quote: Whoever does anything in secret from the bishop serves the devil.
congregational.audited: Smyrnaeans 6.9: 'whoever does anything in secret from the bishop serves the devil.'

passages.author: Ignatius of Antioch
passages.text: If anyone is able to remain in continence for the honor of the Lord's flesh, let him remain without boasting. If he boasts, he has perished; and if he is esteemed more highly than the bishop, he has been corrupted. It is fitting for men and women who marry to make their union with the bishop's judgment, so that the marriage may be according to the Lord and not according to desire. Let all things be done for the honor of God.

presbyterian.quote: if he is esteemed more highly than the bishop, he has been corrupted
presbyterian.audited: Marriages must be made with the bishop's judgment, and esteeming oneself above the bishop is corruption - the bishop judges in matters above the presbyters' sphere.

congregational.quote: if he is esteemed more highly than the bishop, he has been corrupted
congregational.audited: The bishop's judgment governs marriages in the church; the congregation does not order its own life.

passages.author: Ignatius of Antioch
passages.text: Some of you suspected that I said these things because I knew in advance about the division of certain people. But the one in whom I am bound is my witness that I did not learn it from human flesh. The Spirit was proclaiming, saying these things: "Do nothing without the bishop. Keep your flesh as a temple of God. Love unity. Flee divisions. Become imitators of Jesus Christ, as also he is of his Father."

presbyterian.quote: Do nothing without the bishop.
presbyterian.audited: Philadelphians 5.7: the Spirit's charge 'Do nothing without the bishop' gives the single bishop a veto over every church act - incompatible with rule by equal elders, none of whom holds such a veto.

congregational.quote: Do nothing without the bishop
congregational.audited: 'Do nothing without the bishop.'

passages.author: Ignatius of Antioch
passages.text: It is reasonable, from now on, that we come to our senses, while we still have time to repent and turn to God. It is good to know God and the bishop. Whoever honors the bishop has been honored by God. Whoever does anything behind the bishop's back is serving the devil. So let everything overflow for you in grace, for you are worthy. You have given me rest in every way; may Jesus Christ give you rest. You loved me when I was away and when I was with you. God is your reward. Enduring all things for his sake, you will reach him.

presbyterian.quote: Whoever honors the bishop has been honored by God. Whoever does anything behind the bishop's back is serving the devil.
presbyterian.audited: Smyrnaeans 9: whoever honors the bishop has been honored by God, and whoever does anything behind the bishop's back is serving the devil - the single bishop holds a unique, non-collegial authority that no parity of elders assigns to one man.

congregational.quote: Whoever does anything behind the bishop's back is serving the devil.
congregational.audited: Acting behind the bishop's back is serving the devil; the congregation is under him.

passages.author: Ignatius of Antioch
passages.text: Strive, then, to be established in the teachings of the Lord and of the apostles, so that you may prosper in all you do: in flesh and in spirit, in faith and in love, in the Son and the Father and the Spirit, at the beginning and at the end. May you prosper together with your bishop, most worthy of honor, with your presbytery, that finely woven spiritual crown, and with your godly deacons. Submit to the bishop and to one another, as Jesus Christ submitted to the Father, and as the apostles submitted to Christ and to the Father, so that there may be a union of flesh and of spirit alike.

presbyterian.quote: Submit to the bishop
presbyterian.audited: Magnesians 13: with the presbytery present - 'that finely woven spiritual crown' - submission is directed to the bishop 'as Jesus Christ submitted to the Father'; the bishop stands above the presbytery.

congregational.quote: Submit to the bishop and to one another, as Jesus Christ submitted to the Father
congregational.audited: 'Submit to the bishop and to one another, as Jesus Christ submitted to the Father.'

passages.author: Ignatius of Antioch
passages.text: So I have been granted the privilege of seeing you, through Damas, your bishop, a man worthy of God; through your worthy presbyters, Bassus and Apollonius; and through my fellow slave Zotion, the deacon. May I have joy in him! For he is subject to the bishop as to God's grace, and to the presbytery as to the law of Jesus Christ.

presbyterian.quote: through Damas, your bishop... he is subject to the bishop as to God's grace, and to the presbytery as to the law of Jesus Christ
presbyterian.audited: Magnesians 2 names bishop Damas, presbyters Bassus and Apollonius, and deacon Zotion subject to both - the bishop is a distinct officer above the named presbyters.

congregational.quote: he is subject to the bishop as to God's grace, and to the presbytery as to the law of Jesus Christ
congregational.audited: Same structure: a bishop set over the congregation, with presbyters and deacon in subjection to him.

passages.author: Ignatius of Antioch
passages.text: It is fitting for you too not to take advantage of the bishop's age, but to give him all respect according to the power of God the Father. I have learned that the holy council of elders did not despise his apparent youthful rank, but as wise men in God yielded to him. Yet they yielded not to him, but to the Father of Jesus Christ, who is bishop of all.

episcopal-succession.audited: Magnesians 2.3: the holy council of elders yields to the bishop's rank, and honoring him is honoring the Father, 'the Bishop of all' - one bishop set over the presbytery.

presbyterian.audited: The elders yield to the bishop; parity is denied in the very act.

congregational.quote: the holy council of elders did not despise his apparent youthful rank, but as wise men in God yielded to him
congregational.audited: The church yields to the bishop as to the Father who sent him.

passages.author: Ignatius of Antioch
passages.text: Be strong in Jesus Christ. Submit to the bishop as to the commandment, and likewise to the council of elders. And love one another, each one of you, with an undivided heart.

congregational.quote: Submit to the bishop as to the commandment, and likewise to the council of elders
congregational.audited: Trallians 3.13: 'Submit to the bishop as to the commandment, and likewise to the council of elders.'

passages.author: Ignatius of Antioch
passages.text: So be on your guard against such people. And this will hold true for you if you are not puffed up with pride, and if you stay inseparable from God, Jesus Christ, and from the bishop and the commands of the apostles. Whoever is inside the altar's sanctuary is clean; whoever is outside the sanctuary is not clean. That is, whoever does anything apart from the bishop, the presbytery, and the deacons does not have a clean conscience.

congregational.quote: whoever does anything apart from the bishop, the presbytery, and the deacons does not have a clean conscience
congregational.audited: Trallians 7: 'whoever does anything apart from the bishop, the presbytery, and the deacons does not have a clean conscience.'

passages.author: Ignatius of Antioch
passages.text: So I was counted worthy to see you in the persons of Damas your bishop, who is worthy of God, of your worthy elders Bassus and Apollonius, and of my fellow slave Zotion the deacon. May I have joy of Zotion, for he submits to the bishop as to the grace of God, and to the council of elders as to the law of Jesus Christ.

episcopal-succession.quote: he submits to the bishop as to the grace of God
episcopal-succession.audited: Magnesians 2.2: Damas the bishop, the elders Bassus and Apollonius, and Zotion the deacon, who 'submits to the bishop as to the grace of God, and to the council of elders as to the law of Jesus Christ' - one bishop set over elders and deacon in an ordered submission.

presbyterian.quote: he submits to the bishop as to the grace of God
presbyterian.audited: Submission to the bishop 'as to the grace of God' is distinguished from, and set above, submission to the elders 'as to the law of Jesus Christ.'

congregational.quote: he submits to the bishop as to the grace of God, and to the council of elders as to the law of Jesus Christ
congregational.audited: Deacon and church submit to the bishop and to the council of elders.

passages.author: Ignatius of Antioch
passages.text: Make every effort, then, to share in one Eucharist. For there is one flesh of our Lord Jesus Christ and one cup that unites us in his blood, one altar, just as there is one bishop together with the council of elders and the deacons, my fellow servants. Do this so that whatever you do, you may act according to God.

episcopal-succession.quote: one bishop together with the council of elders and the deacons
episcopal-succession.audited: Philadelphians 4: 'one altar, just as there is one bishop together with the council of elders and the deacons' - the single bishop heads the threefold order, as the church's one altar has its one bishop.

presbyterian.quote: one bishop together with the council of elders
presbyterian.audited: One bishop is named separately from and alongside 'the council of elders' - distinction, not parity.

congregational.quote: one bishop together with the council of elders and the deacons
congregational.audited: A bishop stands over the congregation together with its elders and deacons.

passages.author: Ignatius of Antioch
passages.text: So you must align yourselves with the mind of the bishop, as you are already doing. Your council of elders, worthy of its name and worthy of God, is fitted together with the bishop as strings are fitted to a lyre. Because of this, in your concord and harmonious love, Jesus Christ is sung.

congregational.quote: align yourselves with the mind of the bishop
congregational.audited: Ephesians 1.4: 'align yourselves with the mind of the bishop'; the council of elders is fitted together with the bishop as strings to a lyre.

passages.author: Ignatius of Antioch
passages.text: Be eager, then, to use one Eucharist, so that whatever you do, you do it God's way. For there is one flesh of our Lord Jesus Christ, and one cup for union with his blood. There is one altar, just as there is one bishop, with the presbytery and the deacons, my fellow slaves.

episcopal-succession.quote: one bishop, with the presbytery and the deacons
episcopal-succession.audited: Philadelphians 4 (topics text): 'one altar, just as there is one bishop, with the presbytery and the deacons' - one bishop set over the presbytery and the deacons.

presbyterian.quote: one bishop, with the presbytery
presbyterian.audited: One bishop is distinguished from the presbytery he is set over.

congregational.quote: one bishop, with the presbytery and the deacons
congregational.audited: One bishop over the congregation, with the presbytery and the deacons.

passages.author: Ignatius of Antioch
passages.text: The one who is inside the altar is clean, but the one who is outside the altar is not clean. That is, anyone who does anything apart from the bishop, the council of elders, and the deacons is not clean in conscience.

congregational.quote: anyone who does anything apart from the bishop, the council of elders, and the deacons is not clean in conscience
congregational.audited: Trallians 3.7: 'anyone who does anything apart from the bishop, the council of elders, and the deacons is not clean in conscience.'

passages.author: Ignatius of Antioch
passages.text: So it is right for you to keep pace with the bishop's mind, and you already do. Your presbytery, deservedly renowned and worthy of God, is tuned to the bishop like strings to a lyre. That is why Jesus Christ is sung in your concord and in your harmonious love. Now each of you, one by one, become a choir, so that, in tune with one another in concord and taking your pitch from God in unity, you may sing with one voice through Jesus Christ to the Father, so that he may both hear you and recognize, by the good you do, that you are members of his Son. It does you good, then, to live in blameless unity, so that you may always share in God.

presbyterian.quote: Your presbytery... is tuned to the bishop like strings to a lyre
presbyterian.audited: Ignatius, Ephesians 4: the presbytery is tuned to the bishop as strings to a lyre - the bishop is the distinct reference point over the presbyters, not one of them.

congregational.quote: keep pace with the bishop's mind... Your presbytery... is tuned to the bishop like strings to a lyre
congregational.audited: The church acts in concord fitted to the bishop; its unity is harmony under his lead, not self-government.

passages.author: Ignatius of Antioch
passages.text: My chains, which I carry around for the sake of Jesus Christ, exhort you, asking that you may attain God: remain in your concord and in prayer with one another. For it is fitting for each one of you, and especially the council of elders, to refresh the bishop for the honor of the Father, Jesus Christ, and the apostles.

episcopal-succession.quote: "especially the council of elders, to refresh the bishop for the honor of the Father, Jesus Christ, and the apostles"
episcopal-succession.audited: The council of elders is charged to 'refresh the bishop for the honor of the Father, Jesus Christ, and the apostles' - one bishop singled out with apostolic honor above the presbytery he is set over.

presbyterian.quote: "especially the council of elders, to refresh the bishop"
presbyterian.audited: The bishop receives distinct apostolic honor from the elders; he is not one elder among equals.

congregational.quote: refresh the bishop for the honor of the Father, Jesus Christ, and the apostles
congregational.audited: A bishop set apart over the church with the honor of the apostles contradicts congregational self-rule.

passages.author: Ignatius of Antioch
passages.text: If I could enjoy such closeness with your bishop in so short a time, a closeness not merely human but spiritual, how much more do I count you blessed, who are as closely united with him as the church is with Jesus Christ, and as Jesus Christ is with the Father, so that all things may be in harmonious unity?

congregational.quote: how much more do I count you blessed, who are as closely united with him as the church is with Jesus Christ
congregational.audited: Ephesians 1.5: the church is blessed as united with its bishop 'as the church is with Jesus Christ, and as Jesus Christ is with the Father' - the bishop stands to the church in the place of Christ its head.

passages.author: Ignatius of Antioch
passages.text: I, then, was doing my part, as a man fitted for unity. Where there is division and anger, God does not dwell. To all who repent the Lord grants forgiveness, if in repenting they turn to the unity of God and to the bishop's council. I trust in the grace of Jesus Christ, who will loose every chain from you. Here is my plea: act from no spirit of rivalry (Philippians 2:3), but as those taught by Christ. For I heard some people saying, "Unless I find it in the archives, I don't believe it in the gospel." I told them, "It is written." Their reply: "That is exactly what is in dispute." But my archives are Jesus Christ. His cross, his death, his resurrection, and the faith that comes through him: these are the archives no one can tamper with. By these, through your prayer, I long to be justified.

congregational.quote: To all who repent the Lord grants forgiveness, if in repenting they turn to the unity of God and to the bishop's council.
congregational.audited: Philadelphians 8: the penitent must 'turn to the unity of God and to the bishop's council' - the bishop's council is the court of return standing over the congregation.

passages.author: Dionysius of Corinth
passages.text: The one to the Athenians stirs up faith and the conduct according to the gospel. He rebukes them for having neglected this, since they had almost fallen away from the word after their leader Publius happened to be martyred during the persecutions of that time. He mentions that Quadratus became their bishop after Publius was martyred, testifying that through his zeal they were gathered together and received a rekindling of faith. He also makes clear that Dionysius the Areopagite, having been turned to the faith by the apostle Paul according to what is shown in the Acts, was the first to be entrusted with the office of bishop of the church in Athens.

episcopal-succession.quote: Dionysius the Areopagite... was the first to be entrusted with the office of bishop of the church in Athens
episcopal-succession.audited: Dionysius of Corinth (quoted by Eusebius): Dionysius the Areopagite, turned to the faith by the apostle Paul, 'was the first to be entrusted with the office of bishop of the church in Athens,' and bishops succeed bishops in the see - Publius, then Quadratus - bishops traced in a line from the apostles.

passages.author: Irenaeus
passages.text: The apostolic plan stands revealed throughout the whole world; it is present for all who wish to see the truth to behold in every church. We can enumerate those whom the apostles instituted as bishops in the churches, along with their successions down to us — men who taught nothing of the kind, nor knew it, the very thing these people rave about. If the apostles had known hidden mysteries, which they taught separately and secretly to the perfect, they would have handed them over especially to those to whom they also entrusted the churches themselves. They wanted those they left as successors to be very strong and irreproachable in all things, so that by handing over their own place of teaching great benefit would come to those who act rightly, but the greatest calamity to those who fall away. Since it would be far too long to enumerate the successions of all the churches in a volume of t

episcopal-succession.quote: those whom the apostles instituted as bishops in the churches, along with their successions down to us
episcopal-succession.audited: Irenaeus, Against Heresies 3.3.1: 'those whom the apostles instituted as bishops in the churches, along with their successions down to us' - the successors to whom the apostles handed over their own place of teaching.

presbyterian.quote: those whom the apostles instituted as bishops in the churches, along with their successions down to us
presbyterian.audited: Bishops are a distinct office instituted by the apostles with successions, and Rome's church holds a 'more powerful principality' - not assemblies of equal elders.

congregational.quote: to this church, because of its more powerful principality, every church must convene
congregational.audited: Successions of bishops in every church, and 'to this church, because of its more powerful principality, every church must convene.'

passages.author: Irenaeus
passages.text: They insisted that the men they were leaving behind as successors be thoroughly blameless and irreproachable in every respect, so that great benefit would come to those who would act in their place of teaching, while the greatest calamity would befall those who fell away. But because it would take far too long to list the successions of every church in a work of this scope, we will set forth the tradition that comes from the Apostles and the faith proclaimed to humanity, which has reached us through the succession of bishops from the most glorious two Apostles, Peter and Paul, who founded and established the church at Rome. By doing so we confound all those who, in any manner — whether through self-pleasing evil, empty glory, blindness, or bad judgment — gather in any way other than what is fitting. For every church must convene to this church on account of its more powerful principality

episcopal-succession.quote: the succession of bishops from the most glorious two Apostles, Peter and Paul
episcopal-succession.audited: Irenaeus, Against Heresies 3.3.2: the tradition and faith 'has reached us through the succession of bishops from the most glorious two Apostles, Peter and Paul.'

presbyterian.quote: every church must convene to this church on account of its more powerful principality
presbyterian.audited: Succession runs through bishops, and Rome's 'more powerful principality' stands over the churches - not elder parity.

congregational.quote: every church must convene to this church on account of its more powerful principality
congregational.audited: 'For every church must convene to this church on account of its more powerful principality.'

passages.author: Irenaeus
passages.text: Therefore the blessed Apostles, having founded and instructed the Church, handed over the episcopate of the Church to Linus. Paul mentions this Linus in his letters to Timothy (1 Timothy). Anacletus succeeded him, and after him, in the third place from the Apostles, Clement obtained the episcopate. Clement had seen the Apostles themselves and conversed with them; he still had the Apostles' preaching and tradition before his eyes, for many who had been taught by the Apostles were still surviving at that time. Under his leadership, therefore, when a significant dissension had arisen among the brothers at Corinth, the Church at Rome wrote a most powerful letter to the Corinthians. It summoned them to peace, restored their faith, and announced the tradition Clement had recently received from the Apostles. That tradition proclaims one God, almighty, the maker of heaven and earth, the shaper o

episcopal-succession.quote: the blessed Apostles, having founded and instructed the Church, handed over the episcopate of the Church to Linus... Anacletus succeeded him, and after him, in the third place from the Apostles, Clement obtained the episcopate
episcopal-succession.audited: Irenaeus, Against Heresies 3.3.3: the apostles 'handed over the episcopate of the Church to Linus... Anacletus succeeded him, and after him, in the third place from the Apostles, Clement obtained the episcopate' - an explicit line of bishops from the apostles.

congregational.quote: the blessed Apostles... handed over the episcopate of the Church to Linus... Anacletus succeeded him... Clement obtained the episcopate
congregational.audited: Under Clement's leadership Rome wrote 'a most powerful letter' summoning Corinth to peace - one church's bishop-led authority reaching into another congregation.

passages.author: Irenaeus
passages.text: It is necessary to obey the presbyters who are in the Church, those who possess succession from the Apostles, just as we have shown; for they, together with the succession of the episcopate, have received a certain charisma of truth according to the will of the Father (Leviticus 10:1-2). But those others who stand apart from the principal succession, and who gather in whatever place, must be regarded with suspicion, whether as heretics and men of bad judgment, or as those who divide, are puffed up, and please themselves, or again as hypocrites who act for the sake of gain and vain glory (Numbers 16:31-33). All these, however, are far from the truth (1 Kings 12:26-33). The heretics, bringing foreign fire to the altar of God — that is, foreign doctrines — will be consumed by heavenly fire, just as Nadab and Abihu were. Those who rise up against the truth and urge others against the Church

passages.author: Irenaeus
passages.text: The plan of the Apostles stands open to view in every church throughout the world, for all who truly desire to see it; we can trace the bishops appointed by the Apostles and their unbroken succession down to our own day, and none of them ever taught the fancies these people now proclaim. If the Apostles had possessed secret mysteries, reserved for a select few and taught in private, they would surely have entrusted them above all to those to whom they also committed the care of the churches. They wanted those successors to be steadfast and blameless in everything, so that their right stewardship of the apostolic office would bring great benefit, while their failure would bring utter disaster. But to list the succession of every church would swell this work beyond measure; therefore we set forth the tradition of that greatest and most ancient church, known to all, which the two most glori

passages.author: Irenaeus
passages.text: All these heretics came long after the bishops to whom the Apostles entrusted the churches, a point we proved in the third book with every care. Because they are blind to the truth, they are forced to wander off onto one divergent path after another, so the footprints of their teaching lie scattered in discordant, incoherent disarray. But those who belong to the Church walk the whole world over, bearing a firm tradition from the Apostles that lets us see one and the same faith everywhere: one and the same God the Father worshipped by all, the same mystery of the Son's incarnation believed, the same gift of the Spirit received, the same precepts pondered, the same pattern of ordination that serves the Church preserved, the same hope of the Lord's return cherished, and the same salvation of the whole person—soul and body—upheld. passages.author: Tertullian
passages.text: Still, if anyone dares to slot themselves into the apostolic age so they can claim the apostles handed them down—since they were 'under the apostles'—we can say: Let them produce the origins of their churches. Let them lay out the succession of their bishops, running unbroken from the start, so that their first bishop can show an apostle, or an apostolic man who stuck with the apostles, as his author and predecessor. That is how apostolic churches present their credentials: the church of Smyrna reports Polycarp was appointed by John; Rome produces Clement, ordained by Peter; likewise every other church exhibits bishops the apostles installed, as bearers of apostolic seed. Let the heretics fabricate a pedigree like that. What is forbidden them after blasphemy? But even if they forge one, they gain nothing. Their own doctrine, set beside the apostolic, will expose by its variety and contra

passages.author: Tertullian
passages.text: If anyone dares to wedge themselves into the apostolic era just so they can claim the Apostles handed them down—on the grounds that they ‘lived under the Apostles’—we can answer bluntly: let them cough up the origins of their churches. That is exactly how the apostolic churches present their credentials: the church of Smyrna records that John installed Polycarp; the Romans produce Clement, ordained by Peter. In the same way, every other church displays the men the Apostles themselves appointed to the episcopate, the living carriers of apostolic seed. Let the heretics try to fabricate a list like that. After blasphemy, what is left that they would not dare? Yet eve

presbyterian.quote: the men the Apostles themselves appointed to the episcopate

passages.author: Tertullian
passages.text: One last item before we close this material: a warning about who may give and who may receive Baptism. The right to give it belongs first to the high priest — that is, the bishop. Next come presbyters and deacons, but never without the bishop's authorization, for the sake of the Church's honor. Keep that authority intact, and peace stays intact; discard it, and even laypeople claim the right. The logic is blunt: what is received on equal terms can be given on equal terms, provided no bishop, presbyter, or deacon has already been summoned. Learners must not be kept from the Lord's word. (1 Corinthians 6:12) Accordingly, Baptism — God's own assessment — can be exercised by all alike. Yet the discipline of modesty and reverence weighs all the more heavily on laypeople, precisely because those qualities belong to the greater orders, lest layfolk usurp the bishop's consecrated office. Rivalry

passages.author: Tertullian
passages.text: If you want to put your curiosity to better use for your own salvation, then make the rounds of the apostolic churches. In those churches the very chairs of the apostles still preside in their original places, and their authentic letters are read aloud, echoing each apostle's voice and preserving his likeness. Is Achaia nearby? You have Corinth. Not far from Macedonia? You have Philippi and the Thessalonians. Able to reach Asia? You have Ephesus. If you border Italy, you have Rome, from which authority is also close at hand for us. What a blessed church! The apostles poured out their entire teaching there with their own blood; Peter matched the Lord's passion there; Paul was crowned with John's death there; and the apostle John, after being plunged into boiling oil and suffering no harm, was exiled to an island. Let us see what he learned and taught when he contended with the African chu

passages.text: In sum: if it is settled that what is earlier is truer, what is earlier is what is from the beginning, what is from the beginning is what is from the apostles, it will likewise be settled that that was handed down from the apostles which has been sacrosanct in the apostles’ churches. Let us see what milk the Corinthians drew from Paul, by what rule the Galatians were corrected, what the Philippians, Thessalonians, Ephesians read, what also the Romans nearby sound, to whom Peter and Paul left the gospel sealed also with their blood. We have also John’s foster churches—for though Marcion rejects his Apocalypse, still the order of bishops recounted to the origin will stand in John as author. I say therefore among those—and not only the apostolic ones already, but among all that are confederated with them by society of the sacrament—that Luke’s gospel stands from the beginning of its publica

congregational.quote: the order of bishops recounted to the origin will stand in John as author
congregational.audited: A church's standing is proved by its order of bishops reaching back to an apostle - its authority is anchored above and before the congregation.

passages.author: Tertullian
passages.text: We finish by addressing who may give and receive Baptism. The bishop, as the highest priest, holds that right. Presbyters and deacons come next, but only with the bishop's authority, for the honor of the Church. Keep that order, and you keep the peace. Abandon it, and even laypeople claim the right. Since Baptism is received equally by all, it can be given equally by all — provided no bishop, presbyter, or deacon is already on hand. Learners must not be kept from the Lord's word. Therefore Baptism, equally God's judgment, may be exercised by everyone; yet laypeople bear a heavier obligation to modesty and reverence, since those virtues belong to the greater orders, lest they usurp the bishop's consecrated office. Rivalry breeds schism. "All things are permitted," the most holy Apostle said, "but not all things are expedient" (1 Corinthians 6:12). It suffices to act in necessity, when pla

He used to go out, when invited, to the neighboring regions of the Gentiles, in some places to appoint bishops, in others to fit together whole churches, in others to choose by lot one of those indicated by the Spirit. So he came also to one of the cities not far away, whose name some even mention, and after refreshing the brothers in other matters, he looked at the appointed bishop and saw a young man able in body, pleasing in appearance, and fervent in soul. True, the risen Lord gives all the apostles equal authority — "As the Father sent me, so I send you. passages.author: Augustine of Hippo
passages.text: All you who rejoice in peace, now judge truly. Whoever has the love of Christ cannot hate peace. Listen now, you peoples, and agree with us—you who do not hold the see for which you fight unjustly. If your bishops from some one region had a dispute among themselves, whom would you want to judge it except bishops of other regions who were not part of that dispute? But when they had examined the case, they would pronounce for one side; you would never communicate with those who refused to agree with them. Why then did you communicate with these men, who did this before? For they too did not agree with the sentence of the overseas bishops, who judged for us; for they are joined to us today. If Christ the judge should say this, what do you have to answer? All you who rejoice in peace, now judge truly.

congregational.quote: If your bishops from some one region had a dispute among themselves, whom would you want to judge it except bishops of other regions who were not part of that dispute?
congregational.audited: Augustine, Psalm Against the Donatists: bishops of other regions are the judges of a region's disputes, and communion is refused to those who reject their sentence - external episcopal judgment binds local churches.

passages.author: Augustine of Hippo

Before the conference itself, when some of us brothers were talking together about this matter—because for the peace of Christ bishops ought either to exist or not to exist, which we must admit—as we looked around at all our brothers and fellow bishops, it was not easy for us to think of any who would want to take this on and sacrifice to the Lord by such humility. We said, as people do, 'That one can do it, that one cannot; that one agrees to it, that one will not tolerate it'—speaking more from our own suspicions, since we could not see their hearts at all. But when it came to the point that this was done openly, in a council of all together, so crowded with nearly three hundred bishops, it pleased everyone so much, an

congregational.quote: in a council of all together, so crowded with nearly three hundred bishops
congregational.audited: Augustine, Proceedings with Emeritus 6: a council 'so crowded with nearly three hundred bishops' acts together for the Church's unity, and its brotherly correction changes the dissenters - a body of bishops over the churches.

passages.author: Augustine of Hippo
passages.text: All you who rejoice in peace, now judge truly. Our ancestors spoke and made books about it, those who then examined the case, so they could prove it while it was fresh: there were certain traitors of the books of the holy law, bishops from Numidia and not just any from the people. When they came to Carthage to ordain a bishop, they found Caecilian already ordained in his see. They were angry because they themselves could not ordain. Botrus and Caelestius were great enemies of Caecilian, impious, proud thieves, about whom it would take long to tell. They all joined together to fabricate a charge against him; they say his ordainer handed over the holy books. Thus they broke the nets of peace and now wander through the sea.

passages.author: Alexander Monachus
passages.text: For no other bishop of Jerusalem ever arose besides those previously written, nor any other emperor of the Romans, nor indeed was the precious Cross found in any other way. questions.question: May images of Christ and the saints be made, and should they be honoured?
shared_ground: God the Father, in his divine nature, cannot be pictured
Worship (latria) belongs to God alone
Idols of pagan gods are forbidden
The Incarnation made God visible in Christ (shared doctrine; not by itself an argument for icons)

positions.name: Images venerated

defined.source: Second Council of Nicaea, Definition (787)
defined.quote: the honour paid to an image traverses it, reaching the model, and he who venerates the image, venerates the person represented in that image.

defined.source: Confession of Dositheus (Synod of Jerusalem), Question 4 (1672)
defined.quote: the honor paid to the Icon is not at all divided or at all different from [the honor paid to the one who] is portrayed

defined.source: Pope Shenouda III (Coptic Orthodox), Comparative Theology (1988)
defined.quote: venerating icons, kissing them, lighting candles in front of them and kneeling before them. We will try to reply to all these points, showing the spiritual benefits of icons and why the Church keeps them.

positions.statement: Images of Christ, Mary and the saints should be set up and honoured with outward signs (kissing, bowing, lights, incense); the honour passes to the person shown and differs from the worship due to God.
positions.mark: The passage approves honouring an image with outward acts (kissing, bowing, lights, incense), or says honour given to an image passes to the person shown.
positions.first_defined: Second Council of Nicaea (787)

positions.name: Images allowed as adornment, not venerated

defined.source: Apology of the Augsburg Confession, XXIV.51 (1531)
defined.quote: Candles, golden vessels [tapers, altar-cloths, images), and similar adornments are becoming, but they are not the adornment that properly belongs to the Church.

positions.statement: Images may be kept in churches as adornment or for teaching, but no honour is to be paid to them.
positions.mark: The passage allows images in churches for decoration or teaching while forbidding any honour or reverence toward them.
positions.first_defined: Apology of the Augsburg Confession (1531)

positions.name: Images not to be used in worship

defined.source: Heidelberg Catechism, Q&A 98 (1563)
defined.quote: But may not images be permitted in churches in place of books for the unlearned? A. No, we should not try to be wiser than God.

defined.source: Westminster Confession of Faith, 21.1 (1646)
defined.quote: under any visible representation, or any other way not prescribed in the Holy Scripture

positions.statement: Images have no place in churches or in worship; God is to be taught by the preached Word, not by pictures.
positions.mark: The passage says images must not be in churches or used in worship at all, not only that they must not be honoured.
positions.first_defined: Heidelberg Catechism (1563); Westminster Confession (1646)

first_states.text: God forbids an idol as much to be made as to be worshiped. Since the making comes first, so that what can be worshiped may exist, the prohibition of making comes first too, if worshiping is not allowed. For this reason—namely for eradicating the material of idolatry—the divine law proclaims: You shall not make an idol, and it adds, nor any likeness of the things that are in heaven, on earth, or in the sea (Exodus 20:4). By this it forbade the servants of God such arts throughout the whole world. Enoch had gone before, predicting that all the elements, all the wealth of the world—whatever is contained in heaven, in the sea, and on earth—would be turned into idolatry by the demons and spirits of the deserting angels, so that they might be consecrated against God in place of God. venerated.audited: On Idolatry 4: 'Their images are idols; the consecration of images is idolatry,' under a prohibition read universally - 'nor any likeness of the things that are in heaven, on earth, or in the sea... it forbade the servants of God such arts throughout the whole world.' Consecration and honour of images are idolatry.

passages.author: Minucius Felix
passages.text: Consider how mute animals instinctively pass judgment on your gods. Mice, swallows, and kites neither perceive nor acknowledge them; they tread upon them, perch on them, and unless you drive them off, they even build nests right inside your god's mouth. Spiders weave their webs across his face and hang their threads from his very head. Yet you sweep, clean, and eradicate those webs, even while you protect and fear the statues you yourselves have made. So long as each of you fails to grasp that you must know God before you can worship him; so long as you strive to obey your parents without thought; so long as you prefer to join someone else's error rather than believe for yourselves; so long as you understand nothing of the very things you fear—thus avarice is consecrated in gold and silver, thus the form of empty statues is dedicated, and thus Roman superstition was born. If you examine
